item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00029","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C10","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a material structural template: both orders identify a labor dispute between a named employer and represented employees, find that the dispute threatens interstate commerce or essential national interests, create an investigative board under a labor statute, require the board to report to the President within a specified period, and prescribe post-report machinery. C10 and C15 use essentially the same railway-labor form, but C04 is marginally closer because it concerns one named employer and employee representative, like the child. The child adapts that emergency-board framework to a different statute and national-safety predicate rather than copying distinctive language verbatim.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the Carbide and Carbon Chemicals Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Atomic Trades and Labor Council, AFL","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS a dispute exists between The Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization","explanation":"Both begin by identifying a named employer, its represented employees, and their labor dispute in closely parallel terms."},{"child_excerpt":"such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce ... which ... will imperil the national safety","parent_excerpt":"this dispute ... threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce ... to a degree such as to deprive that portion of the country of essential transportation service","explanation":"Each uses an official finding that the dispute threatens commerce and an essential public interest as the predicate for emergency intervention."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall report to the President ... on or before March 19, 1948. Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act","parent_excerpt":"The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act ... for thirty days after the board has made its report ... no change ... shall be made","explanation":"Both establish a presidential investigative board, impose a reporting deadline, and link the report to continuing statutory machinery; the child adapts the details to another labor statute."}]}
